.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Gradually warming temperatures through Monday with increasing
 precipitation chances each day.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...

Multiple shortwave-troughs will traverse the region during the
first half of next week bringing increasing chances of precip.

Air mass remains pretty stable this afternoon per NUCAPS data
from 1744Z. Really don't see much developing today, except for a
spotty shower here and there west of I-81.

Atmosphere becomes a bit more unstable Sunday and Monday aided
by mid-level cooling and increasing warmth and instability and
forcing from an approaching shortwave-trough. Should see a 
gradual uptick in convection each afternoon through Tuesday.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...

Global ensemble models agree on a highly amplified pattern across 
the continent. In particular, a sprawling upper ridge is likely to 
dominate the Desert Southwest into the Great Plains. At the same 
time, below average heights will persist along eastern sections of 
North America. While the core of lower heights stays in close 
proximity to Hudson Bay, an elongated longwave trough maintains its 
presence along the Eastern Seaboard. This configuration would 
support a mainly northwesterly flow regime aloft with embedded 
disturbances sweeping up and over the prominent central U.S. ridge.

Tuesday still presents itself as the most active day of the period 
as the calendar closes on the month of July. Although ensembles 
somewhat wash out the signal of this shortwave, deterministic 
solutions depict this sharpening system encroaching on the area by 
Tuesday into Tuesday night. Aided by modest height/pressure falls, a 
deep wave of low pressure is expected to track from the Ohio Valley 
toward the Delmarva region. Ample instability and vertical shear are 
in play for an active day of severe weather, but at the same time is 
accompanied by many of the usual question marks. Many global 
solutions indicate some ongoing showers on Tuesday morning. How 
quickly these showers and residual clouds scour out will determine 
whether instability is fully realized during the core heating hours. 
As it stands now, damaging wind gusts and torrential downpours 
capable of flash flooding are the main threats Tuesday into Tuesday 
night.

During the mid to late week period, the Mid-Atlantic region sits in 
a post-frontal environment as the earlier boundary lingers near the 
southeastern U.S. Expect reduced shower chances and less humidity as 
the week progresses. The warmest conditions are likely to be early 
in the week as highs push to near 90 degrees. However, this is 
simply close to climatology for late July.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...

BKN035 cigs today and Sunday with isold to sct thunderstorms 
Sunday and Monday.

Tuesday will present multiple opportunities for restrictions. 
This would be driven by any low ceilings from morning showers 
and convective-based issues for the afternoon/evening hours. 
Southerly winds could be breezy at times with gusts up to 20 
knots. A cold front arriving late Tuesday will eventually shift 
winds to northwesterly for Wednesday into Thursday. VFR 
conditions are expected during subsequent days although some pop
showers or thunderstorms could yield a few brief impacts.

&&

.MARINE...

Light winds and fair weather through Sunday. Winds strengthen
Monday into Tuesday with SCA conditions possible. Risk of
thunderstorms also increases Monday into Tuesday.

Southerly winds pick up in strength on Tuesday with channeling 
effects likely bringing gusts to around 20 knots or so, particularly 
across the Chesapeake Bay. Small Craft Advisories may be needed 
ahead of the cold front which arrives late in the evening. Active 
convection will also make for hazardous conditions across the 
waterways. This may include strong winds, abrupt wind shifts, and 
frequent lightning. Behind the cold front, northwesterly gusts 
should be around 10 to 15 knots although some winds could near 
advisory criteria at times.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Gradually rising water levels are expected through Tuesday in
strengthening southery flow combined with near a Full Moon.
Annapolis will likely reach minor coastal flooding early
Tuesday.
